title: Armitage 21 October
when: Online auction closing Wednesday 21 October 2026, each lot at its own time (ADST). The catalogue is going up in parts on Friday 16 October.
deadline: Each lot closes at its own time on Wednesday 21 October; the time is on every card and on the lot page countdown. Bid before the lot's own close.
viewing: Viewing on Wednesday 21 October from 8:30 AM at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay. Phone (03) 6326 2555.
bottom_line: All five catalogues (lots 1 to 600, 601 to 952, 953 to 1286, 1349 to 1677 and 1681 to 1968) are fully checked: every photo was viewed and scoring was blind to the estimate and bids. Lots 1 to 600 (posted Monday 19 October): the find of the sale is Robbery Under Arms, the 1888 Remington three-volume first edition in original cloth (lot 39, estimate $20 to $30): a rebound copy made $6,500 hammer at Australian Book Auctions in May 2024, so keep max $5,300 and flip max $2,650, subject to checking all three volumes at the viewing. Also from lots 1 to 600: a Montblanc Sartorial backpack (18, keep max $410), a carved fruitwood putto (106, $235), a mid-century teak surfboard coffee table (80, $225), a Satsuma tea set (162, $210), Art Deco ceiling lights (239, $200), a Meopta enlarger (552, $170), a Coogan's Tasmania cabinet (528, $155) and pre-war Australian tobacco cards (182, $145). The Singer 222K (142) verifies at $245, below its $305 bid. Two lots with no sold comp but real interest: a Jantzen Sunshine Superman poster (360, dealers ask $1,000 to $1,250) and a pictorial Wallis Island tapa (89). From lots 601 to 1968: Best supported: a 9ct gold bangle, 34.8 g (lot 886, keep max $1,330, bid $700 when checked), a Louis Vuitton Initiales reversible belt (746, keep max $530, bid $50), 15ct cufflinks (905, $490), an old joiner's workbench (1937, $340), a 16-drawer workshop drawer bank (1828, $295), 9ct rose gold cufflinks (904, $260), a La-Z-Boy power recliner (1227, $245), three small Pro Hart hand-coloured etchings (764, 766, 785, about $170 to $185 each), a French carriage clock (661, $210), a Keith Naughton oil (1108, $210) and a Geoff Tyson watercolour (1013, $210). Seen at the viewing on 17 Oct: the Tudor Oyster (883) is a ref 7934 of about 1957-58 with an original honeycomb dial and Rolex-signed crown, keep max $620 on the lowest sold comp, and worth more to the right buyer. Look at the viewing: a Dior saddle pouch (818), an 18ct Hunt & Roskell pocket watch (874), S. Kirk & Son sterling (642), a complete Endemic Flora of Tasmania (683), an enclosed Shoprider cabin scooter (1159) and packs of new Tasmanian oak lining. From lots 1349 to 1677: an early brass-bladed electric desk fan (1412, $210), a Cyclops pedal car (1355, $190) and several James Bond diecast collections ($70 to $90 each); look at the 1975 Mercedes 280S (1349), a Honda Legend coupe (1354), a Lister D-type engine (1677) and a Hot Toys quarter-scale Batman (1424).

assumptions: Every lot in each catalogue was taken from Armitage's public group page, and every lot page and every photo was fetched at full size. Nothing was bid, watched, logged in to or submitted.
Scoring is blind to price: the Armitage estimate, current bid and bid count were removed from the data the scan, rescore and research agents saw. They are shown on this page for information only.
Buyer's premium is 22% including GST on the hammer price, as shown on every lot page. All-in = hammer x 1.22.

Candidates with a blind score of 4 or more got a market pass (Tasmanian past results first: Armitage's own and Gowans' public results, then other auction houses, marketplaces and dealers). Every flagged lot was then re-checked by Opus, which re-read the photos and opened every comp, dropping any that did not match.
Maximum bids use only sold prices in the last 24 months for the same item in similar condition. Melt value for gold and silver is a floor, not a sale, so it never sets a maximum bid.
Gold and silver weights, carat marks and maker claims in the titles are catalogue claims. Check weights and hallmarks at the viewing.
Pickup only from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay. Inbound freight assumed $0 (local).
Sources closed to this session (eBay, Wine-Searcher, Australian Whisky Auctions) were not used directly.
viewing_notes: Lot 25 (closes 12:38 pm): check the edition of The Little Black Princess. The first edition is Alexander Moring Ltd (De La More Press), London, 1905, green pictorial cloth; the 1906 'second edition' is a second printing; the common Robertson & Mullens, Melbourne, printings from the 1920s on are worth little. Dealers ask $1,200 for a 1905 first and $600 for a 1906. Also note the printing dates in the six Bean volumes.

Lot 39 (12:42 pm): Robbery Under Arms. Confirm all three volumes are Remington and Co, London, 1888, in matching green cloth; look for library stamps, missing half-titles or adverts, and cracked hinges.
Lot 883 (5:24 pm): Tudor Oyster 7934. Wind it and watch the seconds hand; check the crown screws down.
Lot 874 (5:21 pm): 18ct half hunter. Ask for the weight in grams and to see the valuation; look for the hallmark inside the case backs.
Lot 818 (5:02 pm): Dior and Prada pouches. Check the Dior serial tag and the Prada Milano plate and serial label.
Lot 683 (4:18 pm): Endemic Flora of Tasmania, Parts I to VI. Check all six parts are present with their plates and the original wrappers or boxes.
Lot 365 (2:31 pm): red acrylic bar stools. Look underneath for a moulded Kartell mark.
Lot 142 (1:17 pm): Singer 222K. Check the free arm, the motor runs and the case has the controller and accessories.
